assumptions.condition: The family \(\{C_j:j=1,\ldots,J\}\) is a finite complete nonredundant ordered-local equality description of the positive nested-Markov model of \(G\).

standard.name: Complete ordered-local nested-Markov property with redundant coordinates removed

assumptions.condition: For every \(j\), the ordered-local kernel-CI semantics gives the disjoint decomposition \(T_j\setminus(X_j\cup Y_j\cup Z_j)=U_j^m\mathbin{\dot\cup}U_j^c\), with \(U_j^m\) marginalized and \(U_j^c\) conditioned.
For \(j\ne k\), the intrinsic districts \(D_j\) and \(D_k\) are disjoint or one contains the other.

novel.justification: Longitudinal hidden-variable chains, nested front-door systems, and disjoint parallel chains have laminar constraint-carrying districts of arbitrary finite depth.

assumptions.condition: After the semantics-designated marginalization and normalization for coordinate \(k\), the recursive-head factor indexed by \(D_j\) appears in the symbolic fixing formula for \(g_{k,Q}\) only when \(D_j\subseteq D_k\).

novel.justification: The condition is graph-checkable from recursive heads together with the published marginal-versus-conditioning split and is satisfied by arbitrary-length sequential Verma chains and disjoint parallel compositions.

assumptions.condition: There is \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{fix},P}>0\) such that every denominator appearing in the ordered fixing recursions for \(C_1,\ldots,C_J\) is at least \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{fix},P}\) on its reference support under \(P\).
There is \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{norm},P}>0\) such that the normalization denominator defining every \(g_{j,P}\) is at least \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{norm},P}\) on the reference support of \(c_j\).

standard.name: Conditional-kernel denominator positivity on reference support

assumptions.condition: Every primitive recursive-head density and its logarithm belong to \(H^s\) on their compact reference support under \(P\).

novel.justification: This proposal-specific analytic class includes tensor-product splines, smooth exponential families, and smooth positive kernel factorizations on compact Euclidean supports.

assumptions.condition: The observed law \(P\) is the observed margin of a causal DAG law Markov to \(G_{\mathrm{lat}}\), and the latent projection of \(G_{\mathrm{lat}}\) onto \(V\) is \(G_2\).

standard.name: Causal latent-DAG model with ADMG latent projection

assumptions.condition: The law of \(Y^\nu\) is generated by replacing only the structural assignment for \(M\) by an independent draw from \(\nu(\cdot\mid W)\), leaving all other structural assignments unchanged.

standard.name: Consistency and modularity for a stochastic intervention

assumptions.condition: The observed density ratio \(\nu(M\mid W)/g_{M,P}(M\mid W)\) is essentially bounded under \(P\).
For each \(n\), observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from \(P_n\).
For every \(n\) and \(j\), the ordered-local equality \(C_j\) holds under \(P_n\) with the semantics-designated marginalization and conditioning split.
For every \(n\), \(P_n\) is the observed margin of a causal latent-DAG law whose latent projection onto \(V\) is \(G_2\).

For every \(n\), the counterfactual \(Y^\nu\) is generated by replacing only the structural assignment for \(M\) by an independent draw from \(\nu(\cdot\mid W)\) in the causal latent-DAG law underlying \(P_n\).

standard.name: Indexed consistency and modularity for a stochastic intervention

assumptions.condition: There is \(\underline\epsilon_{\mathrm{fix}}>0\) such that, for every \(n\), each denominator appearing in the ordered fixing recursions is at least \(\underline\epsilon_{\mathrm{fix}}\) on its reference support under \(P_n\).

standard.name: Indexed fixing-denominator positivity on reference support

assumptions.condition: There is \(\underline\epsilon_{\mathrm{norm}}>0\) such that, for every \(n\) and \(j\), the normalization denominator defining \(g_{j,P_n}\) is at least \(\underline\epsilon_{\mathrm{norm}}\) on the reference support of \(c_j\).
Uniformly over \(n\), the \(H^s\)-norms of each primitive recursive-head density and its logarithm are bounded on their compact reference supports.

novel.justification: The proposal-specific uniform Sobolev restriction is satisfied by triangular spline and smooth exponential-family graphical kernels whose coefficient norms remain in bounded sets.

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\), \(\nu(M\mid W)/g_{M,P_n}(M\mid W)\) is essentially bounded under \(P_n\).
Uniformly in \(n\), \(\mu_{P_n}\) and \(g_{M,P_n}\) lie in bounded Hölder balls of order \(\beta_e\) and argument dimension at most \(d_e\).
Uniformly in \(n\) and \(j\), the fixing weights and marginal post-fixing regressions lie in bounded Hölder balls of order \(\beta_f\) and argument dimension at most \(d_f\).
The population Gram matrices of the cross-fitted tensor-product series dictionaries have eigenvalues uniformly bounded above and away from zero.
Conditionally on each training fold, the maximal \(L^2(P_n)\) error of the learners of \(\mu_{P_n}\) and \(g_{M,P_n}\) is \(O_{\mathbb P}(e_n)\).
Conditionally on each training fold, the maximal \(L^2(P_n)\) error of fixing weights and marginal post-fixing regressions is \(O_{\mathbb P}(f_n)\).
Conditionally on each training fold, \(r_{\mathrm{mean},n}+r_{\mathrm{atom},n}+r_{\mathrm{Gram},n}=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).

standard.name: Cross-fitted finite-series mean, atom, and Gram consistency

assumptions.condition: \(\sqrt n\,\kappa_n^{-1}e_nf_n\to0\).

novel.justification: This target-specific condition records amplification by the corrected joint-fixing inverse; the series-attainability lemma shows it follows from standard series rates whenever the displayed smoothness inequality dominates polynomial weakening of \(\kappa_n\).

assumptions.condition: \(q_n<1\) for every \(n\).

novel.justification: Well-conditioned finite residual dictionaries yield operator-norm projection estimates, while the factor records the observable accumulation of estimation error under near alignment.

assumptions.condition: \(\sqrt n\,a_n(1-q_n^{m_n})/(1-q_n)\to_{\mathbb P}0\).

novel.justification: The condition isolates the cost of replacing population centering by the coherent training-law mean; the implementation-centering lemma reduces it to observable fitted-mean, residual-atom, and Gram errors.

assumptions.condition: Conditionally on each training fold, \(\max_\ell E_{P_n}|\widehat D_{-\ell}|^{2+\eta}=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\).
\(V_n\to V_\infty\).

definitions.name: Semantics-aligned laminar fixing forests
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{LFF}}=\{G\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{NM}}:\{D_j\}_{j=1}^J\text{ is laminar, the published split }U_j^m\mathbin{\dot\cup}U_j^c\text{ is used, and corrected marginal-kernel incidence is a rooted forest}\}\).

definitions.name: Restricted finite-positive Evans class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{LFF}}^{\mathrm{fin},+}=\{(G,P):G\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{LFF}},\;\mathcal O_v\text{ is finite for every }v,\;P\text{ is strictly positive and belongs to the finite-state nested model of Evans2018}\}\).

definitions.name: Positive Sobolev LFF class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{LFF}}^{s,+}=\{(G,P,s):G\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{LFF}},\;P\ll\lambda,\;F_P(0)=0,\text{ and the actual fixing denominators, the }\bar k\text{-normalization denominators, and primitive-head Sobolev regularity satisfy the listed conditions}\}\).

definitions.name: Marginalized and normalized joint fixing interaction
definitions.construction: For each \(j\), integrate \(k_{j,Q}\) over the semantics-designated block \(U_j^m\), normalize the result over \(X_j\times Y_j\) at \(c_j=(Z_j,U_j^c,R_j)\), form \(F_{j,P}(h)=\Gamma_{j,P}^{g}\log g_{j,Q_{P,h}}\), and stack \(F_P=(F_{1,P},\ldots,F_{J,P})\).

definitions.name: Corrected finite-recursion split certificate
definitions.construction: Compute \(L_{j,P}\) from the normalized marginal kernel \(g_{j,P}\), form \(N_P=A_{B,P}L_P-I\), and, after proving \(N_P^J=0\), form the bounded lift \(\widetilde R_P=L_P\sum_{r=0}^{J-1}(-N_P)^r\); on the thereby proved locus \(\kappa_P>0\), select \(R_P=A_{B,P}^*(A_{B,P}A_{B,P}^*)^{-1}\).

definitions.name: Indexed learned-projector one-step estimator
definitions.construction: On each training fold fit a coherent normalized joint law \(\widehat P_{-\ell}\), derive \(\widehat P_{W,-\ell}\), \(\widehat\mu_{-\ell}\), \(\widehat g_{M,-\ell}\), and every corrected fixing nuisance from that law, and estimate \(\widehat Q_{j,n}^{(d_n,-\ell)}\). Extend each projector observably by \(\widehat Q_{j,n}^{+,(d_n,-\ell)}f=\widehat P_{-\ell}f+\widehat Q_{j,n}^{(d_n,-\ell)}(f-\widehat P_{-\ell}f)\), apply \(m_n\) cycles to the causal plug-in EIF to obtain \(\widehat D_{-\ell}\), evaluate it on held-out observations, average the one-step corrections to obtain \(\widehat\Psi_{\nu,n}\), and use \(\widehat V_n=n^{-1}\sum_i(\widehat D_i-\overline{\widehat D})^2\).

definitions.name: Uniformly conditioned cross-fitted series learners
definitions.construction: Use tensor-product spline or wavelet dictionaries with dimensions of orders \(n^{d_e/(2\beta_e+d_e)}\) for \(\mu_{P_n},g_{M,P_n}\) and \(n^{d_f/(2\beta_f+d_f)}\) for fixing weights and marginal post-fixing regressions, fit on training folds, and evaluate all regressions and projectors on held-out folds.

definitions.name: Honest angle-adaptation handle
definitions.construction: Start from sample-split Lepski comparisons of successive cyclic gradients, a nested residual dictionary, and a regularized empirical lower confidence bound for the reduced minimum modulus; use them to select sieve dimension, projection passes, and variance inflation.

statements.statement: The semantics-aligned laminar fixing-forest class is a strict subclass \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{LFF}}\subsetneq\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{NM}}\). It contains \(G_2\), disjoint unions of sequential Verma chains, and fixing forests of every finite depth, whereas a graph with overlapping incomparable constraint-carrying intrinsic districts is excluded.
statements.justification: This locates the completeness result on a graph-checkable class strictly larger than the two-Verma validation graph.
statements.gap: NabiGuoLiu2026, Appendix S4.2, treats one depth-two graph and does not isolate an arbitrary-depth class stable under the corrected marginal-kernel semantics.
statements.consumer: Ananke can recognize admissible graphs by testing intrinsic-district laminarity and corrected kernel incidence.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{LFF}}^{s,+}\), the quantitative lower bounds for the denominators actually used by fixing and by \(\bar k\)-normalization, together with \(s>\dim(\mathcal O)/2\) and Sobolev regularity of the primitive heads and their logarithms, imply boundedness of every required division, marginalization, composition, logarithm, and inverse-fixing operation. Consequently \(h\mapsto g_{j,Q_{P,h}}\) and \(F_P\) are locally twice continuously Fr\'echet differentiable, and every semantics-correct lift \(L_{j,P}\) is bounded. No global bound on \(p\) or on unused primitive kernels is required.
statements.justification: This isolates exactly the analytic consequences needed by joint curve lifting without duplicative global density restrictions.
statements.gap: RichardsonEvansRobinsShpitser2023 defines the fixing operations, but does not establish this local Sobolev \(C^2\) calculus for corrected marginalized kernel interactions.
statements.consumer: The joint-fixing proof can invoke one checkable bounded-calculus lemma for every derivative and lift.

statements.statement: For every \(j\) and every \(h\) in a sufficiently small \(B_P\)-chart neighborhood, \(F_{j,P}(h)=0\) if and only if the marginal post-fixing kernel \(\bar k_{j,Q_{P,h}}\) obeys \(X_j\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}Y_j\mid c_j\). The analytic restrictions imply that \(F_P\) is twice continuously Fr\'echet differentiable at zero.
statements.justification: The lemma makes the nonlinear zero set encode the published kernel conditional independence rather than a full-kernel surrogate.
statements.gap: When variables outside \(X_j,Y_j,Z_j\) remain, a full-kernel interaction is not equivalent to the published ordered-local equality; RichardsonEvansRobinsShpitser2023 supplies the semantics but no Sobolev chart result.
statements.consumer: The joint curve-lifting theorem and any software implementation can use the same explicit marginalization and normalization recipe.

statements.statement: On finite alphabets and \(G\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{LFF}}\), the corrected zero set \(F_P(0)=0\) is exactly the positive finite-state nested-Markov model in Evans2018. Under the natural embedding of counting-measure laws into the mixed-domain formulation, \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{LFF}}^{\mathrm{fin},+}\subsetneq\mathcal C_{\mathrm{LFF}}^{s,+}\). On the same graph \(G_2\), take \(\mathcal O_v=[0,1]\) and \(p_\epsilon(o)=\prod_{v\in V}\{1+\epsilon\cos(2\pi o_v)\}\) for \(0<\epsilon<1\); this smooth positive fully independent law satisfies every corrected interaction, belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{LFF}}^{s,+}\), and cannot belong to the finite-alphabet class.
statements.justification: This gives a second independently checkable comparator while separating finite-state recovery from the genuinely infinite-state extension.
statements.gap: Evans2018, Sections 4--5, establishes algebraic equality completeness and smoothness for finite discrete marginal models; it does not cover compact-Euclidean Sobolev curve lifting, and this lemma makes no claim beyond LFF graphs.
statements.consumer: Finite-alphabet Ananke tests can be regression-tested against Evans coordinates before enabling the continuous corrected-map implementation.

statements.statement: For the explicit edge-list graph \(G_2\), \(\operatorname{dis}_{G_2}(M)=\{M\}\), \(\operatorname{ch}_{G_2}(M)=\{Y\}\), and \(\operatorname{de}_{G_2}(M)=\{M,Y\}\). Hence \(\operatorname{dis}_{G_2}(M)\cap\operatorname{de}_{G_2}(M)=\{M\}\), so \(M\) is validly fixable and therefore primal fixable. Moreover \(\operatorname{mp}_{G_2}(M)=\operatorname{mb}_{G_2}(M)=(Z_1,L_1,Z_2,L_2)=W\). Fixing \(M\) leaves the two non-ordinary kernel equalities in NabiGuoLiu2026, equation (S46), so \(G_2\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{LFF}}\setminus\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{mb}}\).
statements.justification: The certificate makes the causal role of the S4.2 fixing vertex independently checkable from a literal edge list.
statements.gap: NabiGuoLiu2026, Appendix S4.2, uses \(M\) as the fixing vertex for two Verma equalities but does not state the causal-treatment fixability and Markov-pillow certificate needed for the stochastic intervention target.
statements.consumer: Ananke can verify the edge-list criterion before exposing the causal stochastic-intervention estimator on \(G_2\).

statements.statement: If \(G\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{LFF}}\cap\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{mb}}\), every corrected coordinate of \(F_P\) is generated by an ordered ordinary conditional independence, and \(\Lambda_P\) equals the DAG-like orthogonal direct sum of the ordered Markov-pillow score increments of BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022. The genuine-Verma witness \(G_2\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{LFF}}\) has a non-ordinary post-fixing equality, hence \(G_2\notin\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{mb}}\). Thus the joint-fixing theorem has a strict LFF boundary beyond the ordinary-CI-generated intersection, without asserting either full graph class contains the other.
statements.justification: This recovers the published mb-shielded tangent decomposition where only ordinary equalities remain and isolates the minimal genuine-Verma boundary reached by the fixing-specific theory.
statements.gap: BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022, Theorem 2 and Lemma 3, pp. 11--12, derive the ordinary-CI-generated equality model and DAG-like tangent decomposition for mb-shielded ADMGs; they do not cover the non-ordinary post-fixing equalities on \(G_2\).
statements.consumer: Ananke can dispatch mb-shielded LFF inputs to its existing Markov-pillow decomposition and reserve the joint-fixing solver for the certified genuine-Verma boundary.

statements.statement: Let \(G\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{LFF}}\) and let \(P\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{LFF}}^{s,+}\). For the corrected marginal-kernel map, \(A_{j,P}L_{j,P}=I_{\mathcal Y_{j,P}^{\mathrm{eff}}}\), and \(N_P=A_{B,P}L_P-I\) is strictly lower triangular in leaf-to-root order, so \(N_P^J=0\). Thus \(\widetilde R_P=L_P\sum_{r=0}^{J-1}(-N_P)^r\) is bounded and \(A_{B,P}\widetilde R_P=I\); consequently \(A_{B,P}\) is surjective with closed range and \(\kappa_P>0\). Only after these conclusions, \(R_P=A_{B,P}^*(A_{B,P}A_{B,P}^*)^{-1}\) is defined and obeys \(A_{B,P}R_P=I\) and \(\|R_P\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\kappa_P^{-1}\). A chart neighborhood \(U_P\) satisfies \(F_P^{-1}(0)\cap U_P=\{h\in U_P:Q_{P,h}\text{ is positive nested Markov for }G\}\). The implicit-function theorem and bounded-score approximation then give \(\Lambda_P=K_P=\ker A_{B,P}\) after \(L^2(P)\) closure and \(\Lambda_P^\perp=S_P=\overline{\sum_{j=1}^J\operatorname{ran}(A_{j,P}^*)}\). Restricted to \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{LFF}}\), this proves the reverse inclusion left open by NabiGuoLiu2026, Proposition 3.
statements.justification: This is an observable joint post-fixing curve-lifting certificate, with split surjectivity proved rather than assumed.
statements.gap: NabiGuoLiu2026, Section 4, Proposition 3 and the following remark, proves only residual-span inclusion for multiple constraints; Appendix S4.2, equations (S46)--(S51), validates only \(G_2\).
statements.consumer: Ananke can compute the corrected derivative, certify its reduced minimum modulus, and know when its summed residual projection is complete.

statements.statement:
Under the causal latent-DAG and stochastic-intervention assumptions, the fixability certificate and BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022, Lemma 11, p. 24, give \(E_P\{Y(m)\}=E_P[E_P\{Y\mid M=m,W\}]\) for each treatment value \(m\). Integrating this adjustment identity against the fixed known policy yields \[\Psi_
u(P)=E_P(Y^
u)=\Phi_
u(P)=\int\mu_P(m,w)
u(m\mid w)\,d\lambda_M(m)dP_W(w)=P ar\mu_{
u,P}(W).\]
statements.justification: This supplies the graphical identification step that turns the observed adjustment functional into a causal stochastic-intervention target.
statements.gap: BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022, Lemma 11, p. 24, identifies each deterministic fixable-treatment mean; this lemma records the fixed-known policy mixture on the genuine-Verma witness before any efficiency projection.
statements.consumer: The identification formula makes the causal target computable from the same coherent laws used by the one-step estimator.

statements.statement:
Differentiating \(\Phi_
u\), the identified observed-law representation of the causal target, along every regular nonparametric score \(h\in H_P\) gives \(d\Phi_
u(P_t)/dt|_{t=0}=P\{D_{0,P}h\}\), where \(D_{0,P}=
u(M\mid W)g_{M,P}(M\mid W)^{-1}\{Y-\mu_P(M,W)\}+ ar\mu_{
u,P}(W)-\Phi_
u(P)\). By causal identification this is the unrestricted gradient of \(\Psi_
u(P)=E_P(Y^
u)\).
statements.justification: The displayed unrestricted influence function is derived only after graphical identification of the causal policy mean.
statements.gap: BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022, Lemma 11 and the discussion on pp. 23--24, gives the adjustment identification and augmented-IPW simplification for fixable treatment; it does not project this stochastic-policy gradient through multiple genuine Verma constraints.
statements.consumer: The result supplies the unrestricted gradient that Ananke projects onto the corrected nested-Markov tangent space.

statements.statement: For the graphically identified causal stochastic-intervention mean \(\Psi_\nu(P)=E_P(Y^\nu)\) on the \(G_2\) slice of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{LFF}}^{s,+}\), \(D_{\mathrm{eff},P}=D_{0,P}-\Pi_{S_P}D_{0,P}\) is the canonical gradient, and every regular estimator has convolution variance at least \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=P D_{\mathrm{eff},P}^2\). If only constraints in \(I\) are used, then \(\operatorname{Var}_P(D_{I,P})-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\|\Pi_{S_P\cap S_{I,P}^\perp}D_{0,P}\|_{L^2(P)}^2\), with zero loss exactly when \(D_{0,P}\perp S_P\cap S_{I,P}^\perp\). Thus the unrestricted augmented-IPW gradient identified through BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022 is further and completely projected through both genuine Verma restrictions, with a strictly smaller bound whenever the displayed projection is nonzero.
statements.justification: The theorem converts joint curve lifting into an exact information bound and a quantitative cost of incomplete constraint use.
statements.gap: Newey1990 supplies convolution theory, NabiGuoLiu2026 supplies only partial multiple-constraint residual geometry, and BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022 gives identification and efficient influence functions under ordinary-CI-generated mb-shielded geometry; none yields this complete two-Verma efficiency bound for a graphically identified stochastic intervention.
statements.consumer: An analyst can determine exactly how much each genuine Verma equality improves precision for the policy mean \(E(Y^\nu)\).

statements.statement: Under the stated Hölder and Gram conditions, the cross-fitted series construction has \(e_n=O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-\beta_e/(2\beta_e+d_e)})\) and \(f_n=O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-\beta_f/(2\beta_f+d_f)})\). If \(\kappa_n\gtrsim n^{-\gamma}\) and \[\frac{\beta_e}{2\beta_e+d_e}+\frac{\beta_f}{2\beta_f+d_f}>\frac12+\gamma,\] then \(\sqrt n\,\kappa_n^{-1}e_nf_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).
statements.justification: The lemma demonstrates that the target-specific amplified product condition is attainable under familiar nonparametric primitives.
statements.gap: ChernozhukovEtAl2018 gives ordinary orthogonal-score product rates without \(\kappa_n^{-1}\); HristachePatilea2016 does not derive rates for learned post-fixing operators.
statements.consumer: The inequality gives a transparent smoothness-versus-conditioning check before fitting the efficient estimator.

statements.statement: On \(\mathcal H_n^{\mathrm{eval}}\), uniform conditioning of the fitted residual Gram matrices and a first-order perturbation expansion of the residual projection give \[a_n\le C\{r_{\mathrm{mean},n}+r_{\mathrm{atom},n}+r_{\mathrm{Gram},n}\}\] with probability tending to one, for a constant \(C\) independent of \(n\). Hence consistency of the coherent fitted-law means, residual atoms, and Gram matrices makes the observable affine extension asymptotically equivalent to its population-centered comparator.
statements.justification: This converts the use of an observable training-law center into a controlled operator perturbation rather than an exact population-mean identity.
statements.gap: HristachePatilea2016 analyzes population conditional-moment backfitting; it does not quantify centering error from fitted means, learned residual atoms, and estimated Gram matrices.
statements.consumer: Ananke can estimate the three component errors and warn when observable centering dominates the projection remainder.

statements.statement: For every fold, the observable affine extensions satisfy \(\widehat P_{-\ell}\widehat D_{-\ell}=\widehat P_{-\ell}\widehat D_{0,-\ell}\) and \(\widehat C_{-\ell}\widehat D_{-\ell}=(\widehat Q_{J,n}^{(d_n,-\ell)}\cdots\widehat Q_{1,n}^{(d_n,-\ell)})^{m_n}\widehat C_{-\ell}\widehat D_{0,-\ell}\). Comparing each observable cycle with its population-centered affine comparator and expanding the coherent causal plug-in score around \(P_n\) yield \[\rho_n=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\kappa_n^{-1}e_nf_n+a_n\frac{1-q_n^{m_n}}{1-q_n}\right).\] Conditionally on the training folds, \[\|C_n\widehat D_{-\ell}-D_{\mathrm{eff},n}\|_{L^2(P_n)}=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(b_n+q_n^{m_n}+(\delta_n+a_n)\frac{1-q_n^{m_n}}{1-q_n}+e_n+f_n\right).\]
statements.justification: The expansion reconciles a fully observable training-law center with the population tangent geometry and isolates both inverse-modulus and repeated-centering amplification.
statements.gap: HristachePatilea2016, Section 3, Lemma 2 and equations (18)--(19), pp. 929--930, gives population backfitting for ordinary fixed conditional-moment spaces, while BadeaGrivauxMuller2012 treats fixed known projections; neither derives causal plug-in drift for learned post-fixing operators with implementation centering error.
statements.consumer: The bound supplies diagnostics for sieve bias, cyclic bias, projector error, and nuisance drift.

statements.statement: Evaluate every geometric and statistical object at the causally identified law \(P_n\) on \(G_2\), fit each \(\widehat P_{-\ell}\) as a coherent full dominated law, and form held-out gradients with the observable fitted-law-centered affine extensions. Under the indexed model, analytic, conditional learning, target-specific product, implementation-centering, sieve-density, positive-angle, iteration, projector-estimation, envelope, and variance conditions, \(\sqrt n\rho_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\Psi_{\nu,n}-E_{P_n}(Y^\nu)\}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nD_{\mathrm{eff},n}(O_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\Rightarrow N(0,V_\infty).\] Furthermore \(\widehat V_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(\widehat D_i-\overline{\widehat D})^2\to_{\mathbb P}V_\infty\), so the Wald interval based on \(\widehat V_n\) has limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\). The conclusion allows \(q_n\uparrow1\) and \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\) at rates controlled by the displayed primitive conditions. It strictly extends HristachePatilea2016, Section 2.2, Theorem 1, p. 923, and Section 3, Lemma 2 and equations (18)--(19), pp. 929--930, from fixed ordinary conditional-moment spaces and population backfitting to nuisance-estimated post-fixing operators and a triangular causal CLT. It strictly extends BadeaGrivauxMuller2012, Section 4A, Theorem 4.1 and equation (4.3), pp. 426--431, and Section 4B, Theorem 4.4(i), pp. 432--433, from fixed known closed subspaces to random learned subspaces, fitted-law centering error, closing angles, and causal one-step inference; fixed known subspaces recover their deterministic cyclic rate.
statements.justification: The theorem delivers efficient causal inference when the genuine-Verma tangent projectors, their centers, their angles, and their conditioning are learned and vary with sample size.
statements.gap: HristachePatilea2016 treats ordinary fixed conditional-moment spaces and population backfitting, while BadeaGrivauxMuller2012 treats fixed known closed subspaces; neither supplies a triangular CLT, variance consistency, or Wald coverage for a causal stochastic intervention using nuisance-estimated post-fixing operators and observable fitted-law centering.
statements.consumer: Ananke can report a cross-fitted estimate, the explicit empirical variance, and warnings based on estimated angle and reduced-modulus diagnostics.

statements.statement: Can the handle in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}adaptive\mbox{-}angle\mbox{-}handle}\) select sieve dimension, projection passes, regularization, and variance inflation so that confidence intervals are uniformly honest over positive-angle sequences and sequences with \(q_n\uparrow1\) or \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\), while retaining the oracle remainder of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}indexed\mbox{-}projector\mbox{-}limit}\) whenever it vanishes? If not, characterize the minimal honest inflation through an empirically certifiable reduced minimum modulus.
statements.justification: Unknown near alignment and weak joint-fixing conditioning are the remaining obstacles to automatic inference.
statements.gap: BadeaGrivauxMuller2012 establishes arbitrarily slow deterministic convergence at zero angle, but no located semiparametric result gives honest adaptation with estimated post-fixing subspaces.
statements.consumer: A positive answer gives automatic Ananke tuning; a negative answer gives a principled warning and variance-inflation rule.

sampling_model.design: Triangular independent observational sampling with \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\sim P_n\), where each \(P_n\) is the observed margin of a causal latent-DAG model with latent projection \(G_2\).
sampling_model.units: Independent units carrying \(Z_1,L_1,Z_2,L_2,M,Y\) from the explicit genuine-Verma witness graph.
sampling_model.treatment: \(M\) is the validly fixable treatment, \(Y\) is the outcome, \(W=\operatorname{mp}_{G_2}(M)\), and the fixed known policy draws \(M\) from \(\nu(m\mid W)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The causal density ratio \(\nu(M\mid W)/g_{M,P_n}(M\mid W)\) is bounded, and only denominators actually used by fixing and \(\bar k\)-normalization have uniform quantitative lower bounds.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitted coherent full laws estimate the causal outcome regression, treatment density, fitted \(W\)-marginal, fixing weights, marginal post-fixing regressions, residual atoms, conditional Gram matrices, and fitted-law-centered residual-sieve projectors.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 3 proves the summed residual-space inclusion for multiple constraints and the following remark leaves the reverse inclusion open.
Sections 4--5 establish algebraic equality completeness and smoothness for positive finite discrete marginal models.
Theorem 2 and Lemma 3 give the ordinary-CI-generated mb-shielded tangent decomposition, while Lemma 11, p. 24, identifies the mean of a fixable treatment by Markov-pillow adjustment.
Theorem 3 characterizes orthocomplements for models defined by ordinary conditional-independence restrictions.
Section 2.2, Theorem 1, p. 923, approximates efficiency in ordinary fixed conditional-moment models, and Section 3, Lemma 2 with equations (18)--(19), pp. 929--930, gives population backfitting.

Section 4A, Theorem 4.1 and equation (4.3), pp. 426--431, and Section 4B, Theorem 4.4(i), pp. 432--433, give deterministic rates and the quick-convergence criterion for products of fixed known closed-subspace projections.
Optimally weighted sieve minimum distance attains semiparametric efficiency in conditional-moment models.
Canonical gradients and tangent spaces determine semiparametric information and convolution bounds.
Cross-fitting and Neyman orthogonality yield ordinary nuisance-product drift conditions without a fixing inverse modulus.

tldr: Efficient inference for the graphically identified stochastic intervention \(\Psi_\nu(P)=E_P(Y^\nu)\) is developed on the explicit \(G_2\) ADMG with two genuine Verma constraints. A semantics-correct marginalized fixing map and finite recursive-head lift first prove tangent completeness on the larger laminar fixing-forest class. The \(G_2\) edge list then certifies that \(M\) is fixable with \(W=\operatorname{mp}_{G_2}(M)\), so the causal target has the published adjustment formula and unrestricted augmented-IPW gradient. Coherent fold-specific laws, observable fitted-law-centered affine projectors, and a derived implementation-centering error yield a causal one-step CLT, consistent empirical variance, and Wald coverage under learned post-fixing subspaces, closing angles, and weakening joint-fixing conditioning.

project_justification.gap: NabiGuoLiu2026 proves only one direction of multiple post-fixing residual completeness and validates one depth-two graph. BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022 identifies and analyzes causal means under fixability and ordinary-CI-generated mb-shielded geometry, but does not supply complete efficiency projection through multiple genuine Verma equalities. HristachePatilea2016 and BadeaGrivauxMuller2012 treat fixed population moment spaces or fixed known subspaces, not random nuisance-estimated post-fixing operators, observable centering error, and triangular causal inference.
project_justification.niche: The explicit \(G_2\) intervention is a causal target whose efficiency frontier genuinely depends on two fixing-derived equality restrictions, while the larger LFF class supplies the structural tangent-completeness engine.
project_justification.fill: The corrected marginal-kernel map proves split surjectivity and tangent completeness; the explicit edge list certifies causal identification of \(E(Y^\nu)\); and coherent fitted laws with learned affine projectors yield efficient causal inference with explicit nuisance-product, centering, angle, and variance accounting.

related_work: NabiGuoLiu2026, Section 4, Proposition 3 and Remark 5, is the primary structural target: it proves the multiple-constraint residual inclusion and leaves equality open; Appendix S4.2, equation (S46) and the explicit correction in equations (S50)--(S51), is used only to validate \(G_2\). Evans2018, Sections 4--5, is recovered on positive finite-alphabet LFF laws, with no claim over Evans's full graph class. BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022, Theorem 2 and Lemma 3, pp. 11--12, supplies the ordinary-CI-generated mb-shielded boundary; Lemma 11, p. 24, identifies a fixable-treatment mean by Markov-pillow adjustment, which yields the fixed-policy formula after integration, while the present efficiency theorem additionally projects through both genuine Verma restrictions on \(G_2\). RichardsonEvansRobinsShpitser2023 supplies fixing, recursive heads, and ordered-local kernel-CI semantics. PhungShpitser2026, Theorem 3, concerns ordinary conditional independences and only informs the orthocomplement strategy. HristachePatilea2016, Section 2.2, Theorem 1, p. 923, and Section 3, Lemma 2 with equations (18)--(19), pp. 929--930, treats ordinary fixed conditional-moment spaces and population backfitting, but no triangular CLT for nuisance-estimated post-fixing operators. BadeaGrivauxMuller2012, Section 4A, Theorem 4.1 and equation (4.3), pp. 426--431, and Section 4B, Theorem 4.4(i), pp. 432--433, treats fixed known closed subspaces; the present result controls random learned subspaces, fitted-law centering error, closing angles, and causal one-step inference. AiChen2003 and Newey1997 inform sieve construction, ChernozhukovEtAl2018 informs cross-fitting, Newey1990 supplies convolution theory, DíazVanDerLaan2012 supplies stochastic-intervention semantics, and LeeBhattacharyaNabiShpitser2023 identifies Ananke as the software consumer.
technical_internal_limitation: The finite-recursion theorem is restricted to semantics-aligned laminar fixing forests and local Sobolev charts with quantitative lower bounds only for denominators actually used by fixing and normalization. It does not cover overlapping incomparable constraint-carrying districts, merely \(L^2\)-dominated laws, or the full graph class studied by Evans2018. Causal inference is stated on the explicit \(G_2\) slice, and deteriorating angles and reduced minimum moduli are permitted only at rates satisfying the explicit approximation, nuisance, and implementation-centering conditions.
honest_scope: The causal claim is conditional on the latent-DAG causal model, its latent projection \(G_2\), and modular stochastic-intervention semantics. Lemma 11 of BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022 identifies the deterministic fixable-treatment mean; integrating that formula against the fixed known \(\nu\) identifies \(E(Y^\nu)\). Because \(Y\) has compact Euclidean or finite support as a coordinate of \(O\), every fixed-law moment used by the EIF and convolution statements is automatic; the triangular CLT retains its separate conditional \(L^{2+\eta}\) envelope. On finite alphabets, the corrected zero set recovers Evans's positive finite-state nested model only after restriction to LFF graphs. On \(G_2\), the recursion must reduce to NabiGuoLiu2026's published second-order correction and is not a separate novelty claim. The mb-shielded tangent decomposition is recovered only on \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{LFF}}\cap\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{mb}}\); no containment between the full graph classes is asserted. Empty fixing sets recover HristachePatilea2016 population backfitting, and fixed known subspaces recover the BadeaGrivauxMuller2012 cyclic rate. Uniform data-driven adaptation when the angle or reduced minimum modulus approaches zero remains open.
